formats.key: UserDecryptRequestVerification(bytes publicKey,address[] contractAddresses,uint256 startTimestamp,uint256 durationDays,bytes extraData)
effects: Lets whoever holds the private key behind publicKey (in practice the dApp or browser session that made the keypair) have the Zama KMS re-encrypt and read every confidential value the signer can access in the listed contracts.
The grant starts at startTimestamp (in seconds) and lasts durationDays days.
No tokens, ETH or allowances move, and no on-chain code runs in the signer's name. The signature is checked off-chain by the gateway/KMS through the Decryption verifying contract.
extraData is reserved context bytes that go to the gateway/KMS. They move no assets.
formats.shown: The intent says 'Authorize decryption of your confidential data' and names the listed contracts and the number of days. Fields show the contracts, the start date and the duration. The public key that receives the decrypted data and extraData are hidden.

findings.title: The intent and the 'Authorized contracts' label suggest the contracts get a permission. In fact a key holder gets to read the signer's data.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: intent 'Authorize decryption of your confidential data', label 'Authorized contracts' on contractAddresses.[]. The signature lets the holder of publicKey's private key read decrypted values of the signer's handles in those contracts. The contracts gain no right.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Let this app read your encrypted data' and the label 'Data from contracts'. In interpolatedIntent, say 'Reveal your encrypted data in {contractAddresses.[]} to this app for {durationDays} days'.

findings.title: The publicKey that receives the decrypted data is hidden, but no format can make it checkable.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json field publicKey: format raw, visible never. The holder of the matching private key is who gets to read the data.
findings.fix: Keep it hidden, or show it raw as 'Receiving key'. Either way, the intent should say that the requesting app holds this key.

findings.title: No end date is shown. The signer has to add durationDays to startTimestamp themselves.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: startTimestamp is shown as a date ('Valid from') and durationDays is raw ('Valid for (days)'). The cases show '2025-07-01 00:00:00Z' and '10'.
findings.fix: Label durationDays 'Valid for (days from start)'. A computed expiry field would need runner support.

findings.title: metadata is empty, so the wallet cannot name Zama as the protocol behind the request.
findings.fix: Add metadata.owner 'Zama' and info with the protocol URL.

findings.title: Both test cases use a single contract address, so a list of several contracts is never rendered.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json and cases/1.json each have contractAddresses with one entry (0x3C44…93BC). They differ only in the domain chain.
findings.fix: Add a case with two or more contractAddresses.

couldNotCheck: Decryption verifying contract 1:0x0f6024a97684f7d90ddb0faad79cb15f2c888d24 is unverified (no source, abi.json is null), so I could not confirm from code the EIP-712 domain/type it checks or how it uses publicKey, startTimestamp, durationDays and extraData.
